title: Projection-compatible identification of a surjective complex-tower limit
statement: Let R_n be commutative rings with transitions phi_n, A their compatible-tuple limit with projections q_n, and E_n derived R_n-objects with transitions t_n. Normalize the restriction composition comparison chi_n on complexes by the canonical ordinary restriction composition map. Let P_n be complex representatives with markings beta_n and degreewise surjective semilinear transitions u_n representing t_n under those markings. Let P with projections p_n be their termwise compatible-tuple limit. For any specified distinguished Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] with first object E for the restricted E_n-tower, there exists an isomorphism beta:Q(P)→E whose nth projection equals Q(p_n), followed by the canonical exact-derived-restriction factorization and beta_n. No uniqueness is asserted. The derived category, where present, is [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Restrict all $P_n$ to $A$. The maps $u_n$ are degreewise surjective, so the surjective module-complex tower lemma identifies $Q(P)$, with its literal projections, as a derived limit of $(Q(P_n),Q(u_n))$ in $D(A)$. The compatible isomorphisms $\beta_n$ identify this system with $(E_n,t_n)$; the induced isomorphism of products is obtained componentwise, with inverse the product of the $\beta_n^{-1}$. It conjugates $1-s$ to $1-s$ because $\beta_nQ(u_n)=t_n\beta_{n+1}$. Write $B_P=\prod_nQ(P_n)$, $B_E=\prod_nE_n$, $v=\prod_n\beta_n:B_P\xrightarrow{\sim}B_E$, and let $j:Q(P)\to B_P$ and $\delta_P:B_P\to Q(P)[1]$ be the arrows of its Roos triangle. The triangle $Q(P)\xrightarrow{vj}B_E\xrightarrow{1-s}B_E\xrightarrow{\delta_Pv^{-1}}Q(P)[1]$ is isomorphic to that triangle by $(1,v,v)$: the first square is $vj=vj$, the second is $v(1-s)=(1-s)v$, and the last is $(\delta_Pv^{-1})v=\delta_P$. Thus TR1 makes it distinguished, with projections $\beta_nQ(P\to P_n)$. Compare with the chosen Roos triangle defining $E$: rotate both triangles so $1-s$ is their first arrow, use TR3 with identities on the two product objects, and rotate back. The triangle isomorphism lemma makes the resulting map $Q(P)\to E$ an isomorphism. The first square says it respects every projection. No canonical choice of this isomorphism is asserted.

theorem exists_complexTower_limit_projection_comparison

    (φ : ∀ n, R (n + 1) →+* R n)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (q : ∀ n, A →+* R n)
    (hq : ∀ n, q n = (φ n).comp (q (n + 1)))
    (hlim : ∀ x : ∀ n, R n, (∀ n, φ n (x (n + 1)) = x n) →
      ∃! a : A, ∀ n, q n a = x n)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)]
    [∀ n, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R n))]
    (χ : ∀ n, (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q (n + 1))).mapDerivedCategory)
    (hχ : ∀ n (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R n)) ℤ),
      (χ n).hom.app (Q.obj C) ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q (n + 1))).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app C) ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q (n + 1))).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C) =
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app C ≫
        Q.map ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp' (q (n + 1)) (φ n) (q n) (hq n))
          (.up ℤ)).hom.app C))
    (Eₙ : ∀ n, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R n)))
    (t : ∀ n, Eₙ (n + 1) ⟶
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Eₙ n))
    [HasProduct (fun n ↦ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Eₙ n))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (pE : E ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Eₙ n))
    (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n ↦ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Eₙ n)) ⟶
      E⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hE : IsDerivedLimitTriangle
      (fun n ↦ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q (n + 1))).mapDerivedCategory.map (t n) ≫
        (χ n).inv.app (Eₙ n)) E pE δ)
    (Pₙ : ∀ n, CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R n)) ℤ)
    (βₙ : ∀ n, Q.obj (Pₙ n) ≅ Eₙ n)
    (uₙ : ∀ n, Pₙ (n + 1) ⟶
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (Pₙ n))
    (hsurju : ∀ n i, Function.Surjective ((uₙ n).f i))
    (hu : ∀ n, Q.map (uₙ n) = (βₙ (n + 1)).hom ≫ t n ≫
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapDerivedCategory.map (βₙ n).inv ≫
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (φ n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app (Pₙ n))
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℤ)
    (p : ∀ n, P ⟶
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (Pₙ n))
    (hp : ∀ n i (y : P.X i), (uₙ n).f i ((p (n + 1)).f i y) = (p n).f i y)
    (hP : ∀ i (x : ∀ n, (Pₙ n).X i), (∀ n, (uₙ n).f i (x (n + 1)) = x n) →
      ∃! y : P.X i, ∀ n, (p n).f i y = x n) :
    ∃ β : Q.obj P ≅ E, ∀ n, Q.map (p n) ≫
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app (Pₙ n) ≫
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (q n)).mapDerivedCategory.map (βₙ n).hom =
      β.hom ≫ pE ≫ Pi.π _ n
